findings.title: Expired cache rows are reported as active cache
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups every CalendarCache row for a credential without filtering `expiresAt`. Cache reads only use rows whose `expiresAt` is in the future, so once all rows for a credential have expired this API still returns an `updatedAt` value and the UI presents it as a current cache status and offers deletion. Filter the status query to unexpired rows (consistent with `getCachedAvailability`) so the displayed status reflects cache that can actually be served.

findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh the cache-status query
findings.body: On successful `deleteCache`, this mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation below, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, which is the query supplying `cacheUpdatedAt`; `onSuccess` is optional and is not a substitute for cache invalidation. Consequently the deleted cache continues to be displayed as present (and the delete action remains available) until an unrelated refetch/reload, especially because the query disables window-focus refetching.

findings.title: Webhook helper cannot update .env on GNU/Linux
findings.body: The command uses BSD/macOS `sed -i ''` syntax. On GNU sed, commonly used in Linux development and CI environments, `''` is treated as an input filename and the command fails rather than updating `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the `sed -i` arguments based on the platform.
